LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD is for a binary package (`multica-desktop-bin`) that downloads an AppImage from the project's own GitHub releases page. Running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` would only fetch the source archive and source the PKGBUILD's top-level scope. The `source` array points to `https://github.com/multica-ai/multica/releases/download/...`, which is the upstream project's own release artifact — standard practice.

The potentially dangerous code — extracting and executing the AppImage via `./"${_appimage}" --appimage-extract` — resides in `prepare()`, which is explicitly excluded by the `--noprepare` flag and will not execute during these commands. No `pkgver()` function exists (pkgver is a static string), so no code injection is possible there either.

The top-level PKGBUILD scope contains only variable assignments and array declarations with no command substitution, `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or other dangerous constructs. The `package()` function is also out of scope due to `--nobuild`. The `sha256sums` entry appears present for the visible source; any additional entries for `aarch64` would be in the truncated portion and, per standard practice, would not trigger this gate.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Fetching sources from upstream GitHub releases; dangerous code isolated in prepare() blocked by --noprepare</summary>
